body: Which is true according to the passage? The first artist is Vincent van Gogh. According to research, the French city of Arles, where van Gogh spent his later years, had exceptionally bright and intense sunlight. Van Gogh expressed the sunlight, energy, and the joy of life he felt there through bright yellow colors. During his short life of 37 years, he created more than 900 paintings, around 300 of which feature mostly yellow. The series of paintings called Sunflowers includes some of his most recognizable works. Some have said that his preference for yellow in his artwork was due to a medical condition that forced him to see mainly yellow. While this may be true, we can also see his use of blue, orange, and other colors, and these combinations of colors serve to emphasize his joy being conveyed.
solution: ① 아를이 예외적으로 밝고 강렬한 햇빛을 지닌 도시였고 반 고흐가 그곳에서 말년을 보냈다는 내용이 본문에 명시되므로 일치한다. ② 37년의 짧은 생애를 살았다고 했으므로 50세 이상 살았다는 내용은 일치하지 않는다. ③ 900점 이상의 작품 중 약 300점이 주로 노란색을 띤다고 했으므로 '거의 전부' 라는 내용은 일치하지 않는다. ④ 파랑, 주황 등 다른 색도 함께 사용했다고 했으므로 노란색만 사용했다는 내용은 일치하지 않는다. ⑤ 의학적 상태는 '그렇게 말하는 사람들도 있다(Some have said)'는 하나의 견해로 제시될 뿐 입증된 사실이 아니므로 일치하지 않는다.
choices: Van Gogh spent his later years in Arles, a city known for its exceptionally bright sunlight.
Van Gogh lived to be more than 50 years old.
Almost all of Van Gogh's paintings feature mostly yellow.
Van Gogh only used yellow in his artwork, avoiding all other colors.
Van Gogh's medical condition has been proven to be the sole reason for his use of yellow.

body:
다음 글의 첫 문장에 쓰인 While과 쓰임이 같은 것을 <보 기>에서 고른 것은?
Many artists are famous for their particular use of color. While some artists mix interesting and unique colors, other artists use primary colors to express strong emotions. As we walk through our newest exhibition, Colorful Stories of Art, we will explore the use of the three primary colors— yellow, blue, and red—and find out how they were a source of inspiration. Open your eyes, listen to the stories, and try to feel the emotions that the colors show.
보기 ⓐWhile he was waiting for the bus, he read a book on his phone.
ⓑWhile some students prefer studying alone, others prefer studying in groups.
ⓒShe stayed calm while everyone else panicked during the fire drill.
ⓓWhile I was walking home, it suddenly started to rain.
ⓔWhile my dad was watching TV, my friends came to my house to play together.
solution: 지문의 While은 '~하는 반면에'라는 의미로, 독특한 색을 혼합해 쓰는 화가와 원색을 사용해 강한 감정을 표현하는 화가를 대조적으로 제시하는 접속사이다. ⓑ 혼자 공부하는 것을 선호하는 학생과 그룹으로 공부하는 것을 선호하는 학생을 대조하는 '반면에~'라는 뜻으로 쓰임이 같다. ⓒ 화재 훈련 중 침착했던 그녀와 당황했던 다른 사람들을 대조하는 '반면에~'라는 뜻으로 쓰임이 같다. 따라서, 정답은 ②가 가장 알맞다. ⓐ 버스를 기다리며 책을 읽었다는 동일 주어의 동시 동작을 나타내는 '~하는 동안에'의 의미이므로 쓰임이 다르다. ⓒ 대조의 의미로 알맞으나, ⓔ의 While은 코치가 영상을 검토하는 동안 선수들이 스트레칭을 했다는 단순한 동시 상황을 나타내는 '~하는 동안에'의 의미이므로 쓰임이 다르다. ⓓ 집으로 걸어가는 동안 비가 내리기 시작했다는 동시 상황을 나타내는 '~하는 동안에'의 의미이다. ⓔ '우리 아빠가 TV를 보시는 동안에, 친구들이 놀러 우리집에 왔다' 라는 의미로 동시 상황을 나타내는 '~하는 동안에' 라는 의미이다.

body:
다음 글의 빈칸 ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓒ, ⓓ에 들어갈 말을, <조건>에 맞 게 각각 영작하시오.
Van Gogh used yellow ⓐ _____ joy, but Edward Hopper’s use of yellow expresses loneliness. Hopper lived in New York City for nearly six decades, and he created paintings depicting urban scenes that showed how even familiar surroundings could cause the viewer ⓑ a sense of loneliness. Hopper’s Nighthawks is a good example of this. There are four people in the same diner, but they’re clearly not together. The bright yellow walls create a dramatic ⓒ _____ the darkness outside, emphasizing how people can be in the same space and feel apart. In Hopper’s Automat, the feeling of loneliness is even more direct. The yellow lights lead the viewer’s eye to the yellow hat of the woman, and the cool shades of the other colors contrast with the warm yellow, ⓓ that she’s on her own.
조건 1. ⓐ 목적을 나타내는 to부정사 형태로 2단어로쓸 것
2. ⓑ 목적격보어 역할을 하는 to부정사 형태로 2 단어로 쓸 것
3. ⓒ 명사와 전치사가 결합한 형태로 2단어로 쓸것
4. ⓓ 분사구문 형태로 1단어로 쓸 것
5. 보기의 단어를 활용할 것.(중복 사용 가능)
보기 express / feel / contrast / emphasize
ⓐ
ⓑ
ⓒ
ⓓ
answer: ⓐ to express ⓑ to feel ⓒ contrast to ⓓ emphasizing
solution: ⓐ '기쁨을 표현하기 위해'라는 목적의 의미이므로 express를 목적을 나타내는 to부정사로 바꾸어 to express로 쓴다. ⓑ cause는 'cause + 목적어 + to부정사(목적격보어)' 구조를 취하므로, feel을 to부정사로 바꾸어 to feel로 쓴다. ⓒ '어둠과의 극적인 대조'라는 의미이므로 contrast를 전치사 to와 결합한 명사구 형태로 바꾸어 contrast to로 쓴다. ⓓ 앞 절의 상황을 부가적으로 설명하는 능동 분사구문이 이어지는 자리이므로 emphasize를 현재분사로 바꾸어 emphasizing으로 쓴다. 비상(홍) 3과

body:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ, ⓑ의 that과 쓰임이 각각 같은 것끼 리 바르게 짝지은 것은?
The first artist is Vincent van Gogh. According to research, the French city of Arles, where van Gogh spent his later years, had exceptionally bright and intense sunlight. Van Gogh expressed the sunlight, energy, and the joy of life he felt there through bright yellow colors. During his short life of 37 years, he created more than 900 paintings, around 300 of which feature mostly yellow. The series of paintings called Sunflowers includes some of his most recognizable works. Some have said ⓐthat his preference for yellow in his artwork was due to a medical condition ⓑthat forced him to see mainly yellow. While this may be true, we can also see his use of blue, orange, and other colors, and these combinations of colors serve to emphasize his joy being conveyed.
보기 (A) I believe that hard work always pays off.
(B) This is the book that I bought yesterday.
(C) She was so tired that she fell asleep instantly.
(D) The demonstration proved that the theory was correct.
(E) He is the only friend that helped me when I was in trouble. (F) This is exactly the book that I wanted to buy.
solution: ⓑ 밑줄 친 that은 선행사 a medical condition을 수식하는 주격 관계대명사이며, 뒤에 주어가 없는 불완전한 문장 'forced him to see mainly yellow'를 이끈다. (B) 선행사 the book을 수식하는 목적격 관계대명사이며, 뒤에 목적어가 없는 불완전한 문장 'I bought yesterday'를 이끈다. (E) 선행사 the only friend를 수식하는 주격 관계대명사이며, 뒤에 주어가 없는 불완전한 문장 'helped me when I was in trouble'을 이끈다. (F) 선행사 the book을 수식하는 목적격 관계대명사이며, 뒤에 목적어가 없는 불완전한 문장 'I wanted to buy'를 이끈다. (A) believe의 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이끄는 접속사이며, 뒤에 완전한 문장 'hard work always pays off'를 이끈다. (C) 'so ~ that(너무 ~해서 …하다)' 구문에서 결과를 나타내는 접속사이며, 뒤에 완전한 문장 'she fell asleep instantly'를 이끈다. (D) proved의 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이끄는 접속사이며, 뒤에 완전한 문장 'the theory was correct'를 이끈다.

body:
다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
The color blue can produce a calming effect. Even during his days in Paris and New York, Kim Whanki never forgot his Korean identity. The blue sky and blue seas reminded him of Sinan, his home in Korea, which inspired him to create paintings filled with various shades of blue. His use of blue was an expression of how much he missed the place he grew up in. In Tranquility 5- IV-73 #310, the waves of deep blue and light blue dots bring up images of the sea or the sky. Kim Whanki said that he painted each dot as he thought of friends and loved ones from home. On the other hand, Henri Matisse’s blue speaks of freedom. Polynesia, the Sky and Polynesia, the Sea are two Matisse works that have an interesting similarity. In his later years, Matisse had cancer surgery, which left him unable to stand and paint in front of an easel. Instead of painting, he created artwork by gluing paper cut-outs and then painting details. Although his physical difficulties prevented him from doing many things, he still remembered the freedom he experienced while swimming in the Tahitian sea, looking through the salt water down to the sea floor and up towards the sky.
solution: ② 파란 하늘과 바다가 고향 신안을 떠올리게 해 그리움을 표현했다는 내용이 명시되어 있으므로 일치한다. ① 파리와 뉴욕에서도 한국인으로서의 정체성을 결코 잊지 않았다고 했으므로 반대이다. ③ 암 수술로 인해 이젤 앞에 서서 그림을 그릴 수 없게 되었다고 했으므로 일치하지 않는다. ④ 수술로 인해 그림 그리는 방식이 종이 오려붙이기로 바뀌었다고 했으므로 반대이다. ⑤ 타히티 바다에서 수영하며 경험했던 자유를 기억하며 작업했다는 개인적 기억과 연결되어 있으므로 일치하지 않는다.

다음 글을 통해 추론할 수 있는 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?
The color blue can produce a calming effect. Even during his days in Paris and New York, Kim Whanki never forgot his Korean identity. The blue sky and blue seas reminded him of Sinan, his home in Korea, which inspired him to create paintings filled with various shades of blue. His use of blue was an expression of how much he missed the place he grew up in. In Tranquility 5- IV-73 #310, the waves of deep blue and light blue dots bring up images of the sea or the sky. Kim Whanki said that he painted each dot as he thought of friends and loved ones from home. On the other hand, Henri Matisse’s blue speaks of freedom. Polynesia, the Sky and Polynesia, the Sea are two Matisse works that have an interesting similarity. In his later years, Matisse had cancer surgery, which left him unable to stand and paint in front of an easel. Instead of painting, he created artwork by gluing paper cut-outs and then painting details. Although his physical difficulties prevented him from doing many things, he still remembered the freedom he experienced while swimming in the Tahitian sea, looking through the salt water down to the sea floor and up towards the sky.

solution: ⑤ easel은 ‘화가가 그림을 그릴 때 캔버스를 세워 두는 받침대’라는 뜻으로, 영영 풀이인 “a wooden stand used to hold a painting while an artist works on it”가 알맞다. 본문에서도 마티스가 easel 앞에 서서 그림을 그릴 수 없게 되었다고 설명하고 있다. 반면 나머지 선택지는 실제 의미와 맞지 않는다. ① calming은 ‘마음을 차분하게 하는’이라는 뜻인데, “causing people to feel nervous and worried”는 ‘불안하고 걱정되게 하는’이라는 의미이므로 틀리다. ② identity는 ‘정체성, 자아’라는 뜻인데, ‘전통 악기’라는 의미로 잘못 설명되어 있다. ③ inspire는 ‘영감을 주다’라는 뜻인데, “창작을 막다”라는 의미로 잘못 설명되어 있다. ④ surgery는 ‘수술’이라는 뜻인데, ‘긴 항해’라는 의미로 잘못 설명되어 있다. 비상(홍) 3과

solution: ⓐ where → which where는 이미 '전치사 + 관계대명사(in which)'의 의미를 포함하므로, 뒤에 다시 전치사 in을 쓰면 전치사가 중복된다. where 대신 which를 써야 알맞다. ⓒ which feature mostly yellow → of which feature mostly yellow '300 of the paintings feature mostly yellow(그 그림들 중 300점은 주로 노란색을 띤다)'에서 the paintings를 관계대명사로 바꾼 계속적 용법 구문이다. 이때 300은 전체 그림(paintings) 중 일부를 나타내는 수량표현이므로 반드시 전치사 of와 함께 써야 알맞다. 따라서, 정답은 ①, ③이 가장 알맞다. ⓑ '37년의 짧은 생애 동안'이라는 특정 기간을 나타내므로 전치사 During의 쓰임은 적절하다. ⓓ 노란색 선호가 특정 의학적 상태 '때문'이라는 인과관계를 나타내므로 전치사구 due to의 쓰임은 적절하다. ⓔ serve는 'serve to + 동사원형(~하는 역할을 하다, ~하는 데 도움이 되다)' 구문을 취하는 동사이다. 여기서는 파랑, 주황 등 다양한 색의 조합이 반 고흐가 느꼈던 삶의 기쁨을 강조하는 '역할을 한다, 기능을 한다'는 의미를 나타내야 하므로 어법상 적절하다.

body:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 옳은 것은?
Our last color is red, which is often associated with life and energy. R.C. Gorman, ⓐknowing as the Picasso of Native American art, may have felt the same way when he created Navajo Velvet. The painting depicts a woman sitting on the ground, deep in thought. Her figure in a red dress resembles a huge mountain against the background of the deep, starry blue night,
ⓑsuggested the relationship between her and nature. Sometimes red is used to express the beauty of nature. Claude Monet's Autumn Effect at Argenteuil shows ⓒhow the artist celebrated beautiful autumn moments. The bright reds in the painting symbolize the amazing and transformative power of nature. The painting captures the dramatic moment when the forest
ⓓturned bright red and is reflected on the surface of the river. Color is powerful because it stimulates such an emotional response in us. Artists use the same color to express various feelings, so the way we interpret the artwork can be various too. Open your eyes and let the emotions of the artwork ⓔto come to you. You may love it or you may hate it, but art will always take you to a place beyond everyday life.
solution: ③이 정답이다. ③ Claude Monet's Autumn Effect at Argenteuil shows how the artist celebrated beautiful autumn moments.에서 'shows'의 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이끄는 접속사로 how가 쓰였다. 'how + 주어 + 동사'의 간접의문문 구조로, 동사 shows의 목적어절을 올바르게 이끌고 있어 어법상 옳다. 학생들이 what이나 that으로 혼동하기 쉽지만, '어떻게 화가가 아름다운 가을의 순간들을 기렸는지'라는 방법의 의미로 how가 적절하다. ① knowing as → known as R.C. Gorman은 '피카소로 알려진' 대상이므로 수동의 의미를 나타내야 한다. 주어(R.C. Gorman)와 분사의 관계가 수동(~로 알려진)이므로 현재분사 knowing이 아닌 과거분사 known을 써야 한다. 'be known as'의 수동 관계에서 비롯된 과거분사구문이어야 하므로 knowing as를 known as로 고쳐야 한다. ② suggested → suggesting 문장의 주어인 'Her figure in a red dress'가 능동적으로 '암시하는' 행위를 하는 것이므로 능동의 분사구문이 필요하다. 과거분사 suggested는 수동의 의미(~되어진)를 나타내므로 문맥과 맞지 않는다. 능동의 현재분사 suggesting으로 고쳐야 한다. ④ turned → turns 이 문장은 그림이 묘사하는 내용을 현재시제로 서술하는 문맥이다. 같은 절 내 'is reflected'가 현재시제로 쓰여 있고, 앞 문장들도 현재시제로 일관되게 서술하고 있으므로, when절의 동사도 현재시제 turns로 써야 한다. 과거시제 turned는 이 문맥에서 어법상 적절하지 않다. ⑤ to come → come 사역동사 let은 목적격 보어로 동사원형(원형부정사)을 취한다. 'let + 목적어 + 동사원형'의 구조이므로, to come이 아닌 원형부정사 come을 써야 한다.

Kim Whanki & Henri Matisse The color blue can produce a calming effect. Even during his days in Paris and New York, Kim Whanki never forgot his Korean identity. The blue sky and blue seas reminded him of Sinan, his home in Korea, which inspired him to create paintings filled with various shades of blue. His use of blue was an expression of how much he missed the place he grew up in. In Tranquility 5- IV-73 #310, the waves of deep blue and light blue dots bring up images of the sea or the sky. Kim Whanki said that he painted each dot as he thought of friends and loved ones from home. On the other hand, Henri Matisse’s blue speaks of freedom. Polynesia, the Sky and Polynesia, the Sea are two Matisse works that have an interesting similarity. In his later years, Matisse had cancer surgery, which left him unable to stand and paint in front of an easel. Instead of painting, he created artwork by gluing paper cut- outs and then painting details. Although his physical difficulties prevented him from doing many things, he still remembered the freedom he experienced while swimming in the Tahitian sea, looking through the salt water down to the sea floor and up towards the sky. While Kim Whanki's blue speaks of nostalgia for his homeland, Matisse's blue speaks of freedom. Whanki, who lived abroad in Paris and New York, never forgot Korea; the blue sky and sea ⓐ him of his hometown, Sinan, inspiring paintings such as Tranquility 5-IV-73 #310, in which each dot ⓑ _____ as he thought of loved ones back home. solution: ⓐ 파란 하늘과 바다가 그에게 고향을 '떠올리게 했다'는 과거 시점의 능동적 동작이므로 remind를 과거시제로 바꾸어 reminded로 쓴다. ⓑ 주어가 each dot(각 점)이므로, 그가 점을 '그렸다'는 원문의 능동 표현을 점이 '그려졌다'는 수동태로 전환하여 paint를 was painted로 쓴다. ⓒ 암 수술을 받은 것이 이후 상태(서서 그림을 그릴 수 없게 됨)보다 먼저 일어난 일이므로,have를 완료형 분사구문으로 바꾸어 Having had로 쓴다. ⓓ 주어 Matisse가 '~하지 못하게 되었다'는 수동의 의미이므로, was 뒤에 prevent를 과거분사형으로 바꾸어 prevented로 쓴다. ⓔ 그가 타히티 바다에서 느꼈던 자유를 '떠올렸다'는 과거 시점의 동작이므로 recall을 과거시제로 바꾸어 recalled로 쓴다.

body: Which is the best title for the passage? We take it for granted that we should smile for the camera. But a century ago, stone-faced photos were the norm. The smiles we flash for the camera today are about ten times bigger than the smiles photographed 100 years ago. A team of computer scientists analyzed more than 37,000 U.S. high school yearbook portraits from 1905 to 2013. They measured each person’s smile by comparing the shape of their mouths. In the 1910s, lip angles were almost zero, meaning mouths were mostly flat. But in the post-World War II era, people opened their mouths in their yearbook photos. Why did this happen?
solution: ① 20세기 초의 무표정한 사진에서 미소 짓는 사진으로 바뀐 100여 년간의 변화를 압축적으로 담고 있으므로 정답으로 가장 알맞다. ② 미국 졸업앨범 자체의 역사는 글의 초점(표정의 변화)과 다르므로 알맞지 않다. ③ 사진을 디지털화하는 방법은 언급되지 않으므로 알맞지 않다. ④ 졸업앨범 판매량 감소는 글에서 다루어지지 않으므로 알맞지 않다. ⑤ 입술 각도 측정법은 연구 방법의 일부일 뿐 글 전체를 포괄하는 제목이 아니므로 알맞지 않다.

body:
다음 글의 내용으로 추론할 수 있는 것은?
We take it for granted that we should smile for the camera. But a century ago, stone-faced photos were the norm. The smiles we flash for the camera today are about ten times bigger than the smiles photographed 100 years ago. A team of computer scientists analyzed more than 37,000 U.S. high school yearbook portraits from 1905 to 2013. They measured each person's smile by comparing the shape of their mouths. In the 1910s, lip angles were almost zero, meaning mouths were mostly flat. But in the post-World War II era, people opened their mouths in their yearbook photos. Why did this happen? Manners of the past demanded that the mouth be carefully controlled, and a small mouth was considered beautiful. Big smiles were viewed as silly or mean. That's why a serious expression was common in most painted portraits, both in the East and West. Even after the invention of photography, the tradition continued. 1회차 실전 모의고사 The spread of cameras and camera companies' advertising campaigns changed the trend. Early photographers were not very good at getting people to relax in front of the camera, so they were not satisfied with their photos. To popularize cameras, the companies tried to change this by launching advertising campaigns that associated photography with celebration.
Companies wanted to show customers that the camera was a tool for capturing happy moments. They also found that happy images helped their sales, so they began using smiling models in their advertisements. Official images followed suit, and by the 1950s, presidents were smiling in their portraits.
solution: ③ 카메라 회사들이 사진을 축제와 연결 짓는 광고 캠페인을 시작했다는 내용에서, 광고의 방향이 일상 기록보다 특별한 축하 순간을 강조하는 것이었음을 추론할 수 있다. ① 초기 사진사들이 사람들을 카메라 앞에서 편안하게 만드는 것을 잘 못했다는 내용은 있으나, 1910년대 졸업앨범 사진 속 인물들이 카메라를 불편하게 여겼다는 것은 본문에서 직접 추론할 수 없다. ② 큰 미소가 어리석거나 못된 것으로 여겨졌다는 것은 동서양 모두에 해당하는 내용으로, 동양과 서양 사이의 차이는 언급되지 않았다. ④ 1950년대에 대통령들이 초상화에서 미소를 짓기 시작했다는 내용이 있으므로, 공식 촬영을 거부했다는 추론은 본문과 모순된다. ⑤ 미소 짓는 모델의 사용이 판매에 도움이 되었다고 했으므로, 판매량 감소로 이어졌다는 추론은 본문과 정반대이다.
choices: 1910년대 졸업앨범 사진 속 사람들은 카메라를 불편하게 여 겼을 것이다.
과거에는 동양보다 서양에서 큰 미소를 더 긍정적으로 바라 봤을 것이다.
카메라 회사들의 광고는 사진을 일상의 기록보다 축제와 연 결 짓는 방향이었을 것이다.
1950년대 이후 대통령들은 공식 초상화 촬영을 거부하게 되었을 것이다.
광고 속 미소 짓는 모델의 등장은 카메라 판매량 감소로 이 어졌을 것이다.

Edward Hopper Van Gogh used yellow to express joy, but Edward Hopper’s use of yellow expresses loneliness. (A)Hopper lived in New York City for nearly six decades, and he created paintings depicting urban scenes that showed how even familiar surroundings could cause the viewer
(A)[feel / to feel] _____ . (B)Hopper’s Nighthawks is a good example of this. There are four people in the same diner, but they’re clearly not together.

(E)In Hopper’s Automat, the feeling of loneliness is (C)[far / very] more direct. The yellow lights lead the viewer’s eye to the yellow hat of the woman, and the cool shades of the other colors contrast with the warm yellow, emphasizing that she’s on her own.

글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어가기에 어법상 알맞은 것은?
solution: (A) cause + 목적어 + to부정사 형태이므로 “cause the viewer to feel”이 올바르다. 따라서 to feel이 적절하다. (B) feel은 감각동사로 뒤에 형용사가 보어로 온다. apart는 ‘떨어져 있는, 분리된’이라는 형용사 역할을 할 수 있으므로 적절하다. 반면 apartly는 쓰이지 않는 형태이다. (C) 비교급 more를 강조할 때는 far, much, even 등이 사용된다. 따라서 “far more direct”가 자연스럽다. very는 원급 강조에 주로 쓰이며 비교급 more 앞에서는 사용할 수 없다.
choices: feel - apart - far
to feel - apartly - very

Colorful Stories of Art Many artists are famous for their particular use of color. While some artists mix interesting and unique colors, other artists use primary colors to express strong emotions. solution: ⑤의 영영 풀이가 글의 내용 및 어휘의 실제 의미와 일치하지 않는다. inspiration은 ‘영감, 창조적인 생각이나 자극을 주는 것’을 의미한다. 본문에서도 “the three primary colors … were a source of inspiration”이라고 하여, 색깔들이 예술가들에게 창작의 동기와 아이디어를 제공했다는 의미로 사용되었다. 반면 제시된 풀이인 “a dark feeling of fear and worry caused by colors”는 ‘두려움이나 불안’에 관한 의미이므로 inspiration의 뜻으로 적절하지 않다. 나머지 선택지의 뜻 : ① primary: 주된, 기본적인 ② emotion: 감정 ③ exhibition: 전시회 ④ explore: 탐구하다, 자세히 살펴보다

다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
The color blue can produce a calming effect. Even during his days in Paris and New York, Kim Whanki never forgot his Korean identity. The blue sky and blue seas reminded him of Sinan, his home in Korea, which inspired him to create paintings filled with various shades of blue. His use of blue was an expression of how much he missed the place he grew up in. In Tranquility 5- IV-73 #310, the waves of deep blue and light blue dots bring up images of the sea or the sky. Kim Whanki said that he painted each dot as he thought of friends and loved ones from home. On the other hand, Henri Matisse's blue speaks of freedom. Polynesia, the Sky and Polynesia, the Sea are two Matisse works that have an interesting similarity. In his later years, Matisse had cancer surgery, which left him unable to stand and paint in front of an easel. Instead of painting, he created artwork by gluing paper cut-outs and then painting details. Although his physical difficulties prevented him from doing many things, he still remembered the freedom he experienced while swimming in the Tahitian sea, looking through the salt water down to the sea floor and up towards the sky.
solution: ②가 정답이다. 글은 Kim Whanki의 파란색이 고향에 대한 그리움을 담고 있으며, Matisse의 파란색은 자유를 표현한다고 설명하고 있으므로, 두 화가가 파란색에 부여한 서로 다른 의미가 글의 주제로 가장 적절하다. ① 파란색이 일상에서 안정감을 준다는 내용은 도입부의 한 문장으로만 언급될 뿐, 글 전체의 주제를 포괄하지 못한다. ③ Matisse가 신체적 어려움을 극복한 방식은 Matisse를 소개하는 일부 사례일 뿐, 글의 핵심 주제는 아니다. ④ Sinan의 풍경에서 영감을 받은 점은 Kim Whanki의 점 기법을 설명하기 위한 세부 사항일 뿐, 글 전체 주제를 담지 못한다. ⑤ 종이 오리기 기법은 Matisse의 신체 상황을 설명하는 부수적 내용으로, 글의 중심 주제와 거리가 멀다.
choices: The calming influence of the color blue in daily life
Different meanings of blue expressed by two artists
How Matisse overcame physical difficulties through art
Kim Whanki's use of dots inspired by Sinan's landscape
The role of paper cut-outs in modern abstract painting

solution: ⓑ what → how "find out" 뒤에 이어지는 절 "they were a source of inspiration"은 주어(they)와 동사(were), 보어(a source of inspiration)를 모두 갖춘 완전한 문장 구조이다. 따라서 명사절을 이끄는 접속사로 '어떻게 ~였는지'의 의미를 나타내는 how가 적절하다. what은 명사절 안에서 주어나 목적어 역할을 해야 하는데, 뒤 절이 이미 완전하므로 what은 올 수 없다. ⓓ conveying → being conveyed "his joy"는 색깔들의 조합에 의해 '전달되는' 대상이므로 수동의 의미를 나타내야 한다. 따라서 능동형 현재분사 conveying이 아니라 수동의 의미를 가진 being conveyed가 올바르다. ⓐ "unique"는 앞의 형용사 "interesting"과 병렬 구조를 이루며 명사 "colors"를 수식하는 형용사로 올바르게 쓰였다. ⓒ "of which"는 선행사 "900 paintings" 중 일부인 "300"을 나타내는 [수사 + of which] 구조의 관계대명사구로 올바르게 쓰였다. ⓔ "depicting"은 앞의 명사 "paintings"를 수식하는 현재분사로, paintings가 능동적으로 도시 장면을 묘사하는 주체이므로 올바르게 쓰였다.

The color blue can produce a calming effect. Even during his days in Paris and New York, Kim Whanki never forgot his Korean identity. The blue sky and blue seas reminded him of Sinan, his home in Korea, which inspired him to create paintings filled with various shades of blue. His use of blue was an expression of how much he missed the place he grew up in. In Tranquility 5-IV-73 #310, the waves of deep blue and light blue dots
ⓐevoke images of the sea or the sky. Kim Whanki said that he painted each dot as he thought of friends and loved ones from home. On the other hand, Henri Matisse's blue speaks of freedom. Polynesia, the Sky and Polynesia, the Sea are two Matisse works that have an interesting similarity. In his later years, Matisse had cancer surgery, which left him unable to stand and paint in front of an easel. Instead of painting, he created artwork by gluing paper cut-outs and then painting details. Although his physical difficulties ⓑkept him from doing many things, he still remembered the freedom he experienced while swimming in the Tahitian sea, looking through the salt water down to the sea floor and up towards the sky. Our last color is red, which is often associated with life and energy. R.C. Gorman, known as the Picasso of Native American art, may have felt the same way when he created Navajo Velvet. The painting depicts a woman sitting on the ground, deep in thought. Her ⓒimage in a red dress resembles a huge mountain against the background of the deep, starry blue night, suggesting the relationship between her and nature. Sometimes red is used to express the beauty of nature. Claude Monet's Autumn Effect at Argenteuil shows how the artist celebrated beautiful autumn moments. The bright reds in the painting symbolize the amazing and ⓓtransferable power of nature. The painting ⓔcaptures the dramatic moment when the forest turns bright red and is reflected on the surface of the river.

다음 글의 내용으로 추론할 수 있는 것은?
Many artists are famous for their particular use of color. While some artists mix interesting and unique colors, other artists use primary colors to express strong emotions. As we walk through our newest exhibition, Colorful Stories of Art, we will explore the use of the three primary colors— yellow, blue, and red—and find out how they were a source of inspiration. Open your eyes, listen to the stories, and try to feel the emotions that the colors show. The first artist is Vincent van Gogh. According to research, the French city of Arles, where van Gogh spent his later years, had exceptionally bright and intense sunlight. Van Gogh expressed the sunlight, energy, and the joy of life he felt there through bright yellow colors. During his short life of 37 years, he created more than 900 paintings, around 300 of which feature mostly yellow. The series of paintings called Sunflowers includes some of his most recognizable works. Some have said that his preference for yellow in his artwork was due to a medical condition that forced him to see mainly yellow. While this may be true, we can also see his use of blue, orange, and other colors, and these combinations of colors serve to emphasize his joy being conveyed. Van Gogh used yellow to express joy, but Edward Hopper's use of yellow expresses loneliness. Hopper lived in New York City for nearly six decades, and he created paintings depicting urban scenes that showed how even familiar surroundings could cause the viewer to feel a sense of loneliness. Hopper's Nighthawks is a good example of this. There are four people in the same diner, but they're clearly not together. The bright yellow walls create a dramatic contrast to the darkness outside, emphasizing how people can be in the same space and feel apart. In Hopper's Automat, the feeling of loneliness is even more direct. The yellow lights lead the viewer's eye to the yellow hat of the woman, and the cool shades of the other colors contrast with the warm yellow, emphasizing that she's on her own.
solution: ⑤ 본문은 Hopper의 Automat에서 노란 조명이 여성의 노란 모자로 시선을 유도하고, 다른 색들의 차가운 색조가 따뜻한 노란색과 대비를 이루어 여성이 혼자임을 강조한다고 설명한다. 이를 통해 따뜻한 노란색과 차가운 색조의 대비가 그림 속 여성의 고독감을 강조한다고 추론할 수 있다. ① 본문은 이 전시회가 세 가지 primary colors의 사용을 탐구한다고 했으므로, 혼합색 작품을 중점적으로 다룬다는 것은 추론할 수 없다. ② 본문은 van Gogh가 Arles에서 햇빛과 생명의 기쁨을 노란색으로 표현했다고만 서술하며, Arles 이전의 색채 선호에 대해서는 언급하지 않으므로 추론할 수 없다. ③ van Gogh가 900점 이상의 그림을 그렸고 그 중 약 300점이 주로 노란색을 사용했다고 명시되어 있으므로, 600점 이상이 노란색 위주라는 것은 사실과 다르다. ④ 본문은 Nighthawks 속 네 인물이 같은 식당에 있지만 명백히 함께가 아니라고 했으므로, 친밀한 관계라는 진술은 본문 내용과 모순된다.

solution: ⓑ feeling → felt 관계대명사가 생략된 목적격 관계절 'he there'에서 동사가 필요하다. 문맥상 '그가 그곳에서 느꼈던 삶의 기쁨'이라는 의미이므로, 분사형 feeling이 아니라 과거 시제 동사 felt가 와야 한다. feeling은 이 자리에서 관계절의 정동사 역할을 할 수 없다. ⓓ calling → called 'The series of paintings'를 뒤에서 수식하는 분사구이다. 'Sunflowers'라는 이름으로 불리는 것은 paintings이므로, paintings와 call의 관계는 수동(paintings are called Sunflowers)이다. 따라서 능동의 현재분사 calling이 아니라 수동의 과거분사 called가 와야 한다. ⓐ 'the French city of Arles'를 선행사로 하는 관계절에서 '반 고흐가 만년을 보낸 장소'라는 의미이므로, 장소를 나타내는 관계부사 where가 올바르게 쓰였다. ⓒ 'around 300 of which feature mostly yellow'는 「of which + 주어 + 동사」 구조의 관계절로, 선행사 '900 paintings' 중 300점을 가리킨다. 주어가 복수(300)이므로 동사 feature(복수 일치)도 올바르게 쓰였다. ⓔ 'serve to-부정사' 구조는 '~하는 역할을 하다'라는 의미의 관용 표현으로, to emphasize가 올바르게 쓰였다.

다음 글을 읽고 대답할 수 없는 질문은?
Many artists are famous for their particular use of color. While some artists mix interesting and unique colors, other artists use primary colors to express strong emotions. As we walk through our newest exhibition, Colorful Stories of Art, we will explore the use of the three primary colors— yellow, blue, and red—and find out how they were a source of inspiration. Open your eyes, listen to the stories, and try to feel the emotions that the colors show. The first artist is Vincent van Gogh. According to research, the French city of Arles, where van Gogh spent his later years, had exceptionally bright and intense sunlight. Van Gogh expressed the sunlight, energy, and the joy of life he felt there through bright yellow colors. During his short life of 37 years, he created more than 900 paintings, around 300 of which feature mostly yellow. The series of paintings called Sunflowers includes some of his most recognizable works. Some have said that his preference for yellow in his artwork was due to a medical condition that forced him to see mainly yellow. While this may be true, we can also see his use of blue, orange, and other colors, and these combinations of colors serve to emphasize his joy being conveyed. Van Gogh used yellow to express joy, but Edward Hopper's use of yellow expresses loneliness. Hopper lived in New York City for nearly six decades, and he created paintings depicting urban scenes that showed how even familiar surroundings could cause the viewer to feel a sense of loneliness. Hopper's Nighthawks is a good example of this. There are four people in the same diner, but they're clearly not together. The bright yellow walls create a dramatic contrast to the darkness outside, emphasizing how people can be in the same space and feel apart. In Hopper's Automat, the feeling of loneliness is even more direct. The yellow lights lead the viewer's eye to the yellow hat of the woman, and the cool shades of the other colors contrast with the warm yellow, emphasizing that she's on her own.
solution: ③ 본문은 van Gogh가 말년을 Arles에서 보냈다는 사실만 언급할 뿐, 그가 Arles로 이주한 이유는 전혀 설명하지 않으므로 이 질문에는 답할 수 없다. ① 본문 도입부에서 전시회가 탐구하는 세 가지 원색이 노란색, 파란색, 빨간색임을 밝히고 있으므로 답할 수 있다. ② 본문에서 van Gogh가 37년의 짧은 생애 동안 900점 이상의 그림을 그렸다고 명시하고 있으므로 답할 수 있다. ④ 본문에서 Hopper의 노란색 사용은 고독감을 표현한다고 명확히 서술하고 있으므로 답할 수 있다. ⑤ 본문에서 Nighthawks에 같은 식당 안에 네 명의 인물이 있다고 언급하고 있으므로 답할 수 있다.
choices: What are the three primary colors explored in the exhibition?
How many paintings did van Gogh create during his lifetime?
Why did van Gogh move to the French city of Arles?
What emotion does Hopper's use of yellow mainly express?
How many people are depicted in Hopper's Nighthawks?

body:
다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
The color blue can produce a calming effect. Even during his days in Paris and New York, Kim Whanki never forgot his Korean identity. The blue sky and blue seas reminded him of Sinan, his home in Korea, which inspired him to create paintings filled with various shades of blue. His use of blue was an expression of how much he missed the place he grew up in. In Tranquility 5- IV-73 #310, the waves of deep blue and light blue dots bring up images of the sea or the sky. Kim Whanki said that he painted each dot as he thought of friends and loved ones from home. On the other hand, Henri Matisse’s blue speaks of freedom. Polynesia, the Sky and Polynesia, the Sea are two Matisse works that have an interesting similarity. In his later years, Matisse had cancer surgery, which left him unable to stand and paint in front of an easel. Instead of painting, he created artwork by gluing paper cut-outs and then painting details. Although his physical difficulties prevented him from doing many things, he still remembered the freedom he experienced while swimming in the Tahitian sea, looking through the salt water down to the sea floor and up towards the sky.
solution: ② 이 글은 김환기의 파랑이 고향에 대한 그리움을, 마티스의 파랑이 자유를 표현한다는 대조를 중심으로 두 화가가 같은 색에 서로 다른 의미를 담아낸 방식을 다루므로 정답으로 가장 알맞다. ① 색이 주는 진정 효과는 글 도입부의 일반적 진술일 뿐, 두 화가의 개별적 색채 의미를 다루는 글 전체를 포괄하지 못하므로 알맞지 않다. ③ 마티스의 신체적 어려움과 창작 방식 전환은 글 후반부의 일부 내용일 뿐, 김환기에 관한 내용을 포괄하지 못하므로 글 전체의 주제로는 알맞지 않다. ④ 두 화가의 전통적 화법에 대한 설명은 본문에 언급되지 않으므로 알맞지 않다. ⑤ 종이 오려 붙이기 예술의 역사는 마티스 개인의 창작 방식으로 언급될 뿐, 20세기 전체의 역사를 다루는 내용이 아니므로 알맞지 않다.

Our last color is red, which is often associated with life and energy. R.C. Gorman, known as the Picasso of Native American art, may have felt the same way when he created Navajo Velvet. The painting depicts a woman sitting on the ground, deep in thought. Her figure in a red dress resembles a huge mountain against the background of the deep, starry blue night, suggesting the relationship between her and nature. Sometimes red is used to express the beauty of nature. Claude Monet's Autumn Effect at Argenteuil shows how the artist celebrated beautiful autumn moments. The bright reds in the painting symbolize the amazing and transformative power of nature. The painting captures the dramatic moment when the forest turns bright red and is reflected on the surface of the river. Color is powerful because it stimulates such an emotional response in us. Artists use the same color to express various feelings, so the way we interpret the artwork can be various too. When you truly look at a painting, (A) _____ .

윗글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

body:
다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오.
Our last color is red, which is often associated with life and energy. R.C. Gorman, known as the Picasso of Native American art, may have felt the same way when he created Navajo Velvet. The painting depicts a woman sitting on the ground, deep in thought. Her figure in a red dress resembles a huge mountain against the background of the deep, starry blue night, suggesting the relationship between her and nature. Sometimes red is used to express the beauty of nature. Claude Monet's Autumn Effect at Argenteuil shows how the artist celebrated beautiful autumn moments. The bright reds in the painting symbolize the amazing and transformative power of nature. The painting captures the dramatic moment when the forest turns bright red and is reflected on the surface of the river. Color is powerful because it stimulates such an emotional response in us. Artists use the same color to express various feelings, so the way we interpret the artwork can be various too. When you truly look at a painting, (A) _____ .

윗글의 빈칸 (A)에 들어갈 내용으로 가장 적절한 것은?
solution: 예술은 우리의 감정적 반응을 자극하고 일상을 넘어선 곳으로 데려다준다는 내용으로, 그림을 볼 때 영감을 준다는 내용이 와야 할 것이다. 따라서 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은 ② ‘그것은 당신의 마음에 영감을 주고 당신을 다른 세계로 이끈다’이다.

it inspires your mind and draws you into a different world

body:
다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오.
The color blue can produce a calming effect. Even during his days in Paris and New York, Kim Whanki never forgot his Korean identity. ⓐThe blue sky and blue seas reminded him of Sinan, his home in Korea, which inspired him to create paintings filled with various shades of blue. ⓑHis use of blue was an expression of how much he missed the place he grew up in. ⓒIn Tranquility 5-IV-73 #310, the waves of deep blue and light blue dots bring up images of the sea or the sky. Kim Whanki said that he painted each dot as he thought of friends and loved ones from home. On the other hand, Henri Matisse’s blue speaks of freedom. Polynesia, the Sky and Polynesia, the Sea are two Matisse works that have an interesting similarity. ⓓIn his later years, Matisse had cancer surgery, which left him to be unable to stand and paint in front of an easel. Instead of painting, he created artwork by gluing paper cut-outs and then painting details. ⓔAlthough his physical difficulties prevented him from doing many things, he still remembered the freedom he experienced while swimming in the Tahitian sea, looking through the salt water down to the sea floor and up towards the sky.

윗글에서 추론할 수 있는 내용으로 적절하지 않은 것은?
solution: Matisse는 암 수술 이후 이젤 앞에 서서 그림을 그릴 수 없게 되자, 종이를 오려 붙이는 컷아웃 기법을 사용하여 예술 활동을 지속했다고 명시했으므로, 추론할 수 있는 내용으로 적절하지 않은 것은 ④ 'Matisse는 수술로 인해 신체 건강이 악화된 이후 예술 창작을 중단했다.'이다.
choices: Kim Whanki maintained his Korean identity even while living abroad in New York.
Each dot in Kim Whanki's work represents a person he missed from his home.
Henri Matisse's works share a thematic or visual similarity.
Matisse stopped creating art after his physical health deteriorated due to surgery.
Matisse's memory of swimming in the Tahitian sea served as an inspiration for his art.

body:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?
We take it for granted that we should smile for the camera. But a century ago, stone-faced photos were the norm. The smiles we flash for the camera today are about ten times ⓐbigger than the smiles photographed 100 years ago. A team of computer scientists analyzed more than 37,000 U.S. high school yearbook portraits from 1905 to 2013. They measured each person's smile ⓑby comparing the shape of their mouths. In the 1910s, lip angles were almost zero, meaning mouths were mostly flat. But in the post-World War II era, people opened their mouths in their yearbook photos. Why did this happen? Manners of the past demanded that the mouth
ⓒis carefully controlled, and a small mouth was considered beautiful. Big smiles were viewed as silly or mean. That's why a serious expression was common in most painted portraits, both in the East and West. Even after the invention of photography, the tradition continued. The spread of cameras and camera companies' advertising campaigns changed the trend. Early photographers were not very good at getting people ⓓto relax in front of the camera, so they were not satisfied with their photos. To popularize cameras, the companies tried to change this by launching advertising campaigns that associated photography with celebration. Companies wanted to show customers that the camera was a tool for capturing happy moments. They also found that happy images helped their sales, so they began using ⓔsmiling models in their advertisements. Official images followed suit, and by the 1950s, presidents were smiling in their portraits.
solution: ③ is → be 'demanded that the mouth is carefully controlled'에서 demand는 요구·주장·제안을 나타내는 동사로, that절에 가정법 현재(동사원형)를 요구한다. 따라서 is를 동사원형 be로 고쳐야 한다. ① 'ten times bigger than'에서 배수 표현 뒤에 비교급 형용사 bigger가 올바르게 쓰였다. ② 'by comparing'은 전치사 by의 목적어로 동명사 comparing이 올바르게 쓰였다. ④ 'get + 목적어 + to부정사' 구조로, get people to relax에서 to relax가 올바르게 쓰였다. ⑤ smiling은 현재분사로서 명사 models를 앞에서 수식하는 형용사 역할을 하며 올바르게 쓰였다.
choices: ⓔ 유형보충독해1

We take it for granted that we should smile for the camera. But a century ago, stone-faced photos were the norm. Manners of the past demanded that the mouth be carefully controlled, and a small mouth was considered beautiful. Big smiles were viewed as silly or mean. That's why a serious expression was common in most painted portraits, both in the East and West. Even after the invention of photography, the tradition continued. The spread of cameras and camera companies' advertising campaigns changed the trend. Early photographers were not very good at getting people to relax in front of the camera, so they were not satisfied with their photos. To popularize cameras, the companies tried to change this by launching advertising campaigns that associated photography with celebration. Companies wanted to show customers that the camera was a tool for capturing happy moments. They also found that happy images helped their sales, so they began using smiling models in their advertisements. Official images followed suit, and by the 1950s, presidents were smiling in their portraits.
solution: ② 컴퓨터 과학자들의 졸업앨범 사진 분석을 출발점으로, 과거의 예절 문화와 카메라 회사들의 광고 캠페인이 사진 속 미소 규범을 어떻게 변화시켰는지 역사적·사회적 흐름 전체를 설명하고 있으므로, 글의 목적으로 가장 적절하다. ① 카메라 기술의 발전사를 기록하는 것은 이 글의 목적이 아니며, 기술 변천에 대한 내용은 언급되지 않았다. ③ 동서양 초상화의 예술적 기준 분석은 과거 문화 관습을 배경으로 제시하는 부분 사례일 뿐, 글 전체의 목적은 아니다. ④ 졸업앨범 사진이 문화적 정체성을 반영해야 한다는 주장은 본문에서 언급되지 않았다. ⑤ 글의 핵심은 카메라 회사의 광고를 홍보하는 것이 아니라, 광고 캠페인이 미소 문화 변화에 미친 영향을 설명하는 것이다.

answer: Big smiles were viewed as silly or mean.

The first artist is Vincent van Gogh. According to research, the French city of Arles, where van Gogh spent his later years, had exceptionally bright and intense sunlight. Van Gogh expressed the sunlight, energy, and the joy of life he felt there through bright yellow colors. During his short life of 37 years, he created more than 900 paintings, around 300 of which feature mostly yellow. The series of paintings called Sunflowers includes some of his most recognizable works. Some have said that his preference for yellow in his artwork was due to a medical condition that forced him to see mainly yellow. While this may be true, we can also see his use of blue, orange, and other colors, and these combinations of colors serve to emphasize his joy being conveyed. Van Gogh used yellow to express joy, but Edward Hopper's use of yellow expresses loneliness. Hopper lived in New York City for nearly six decades, and he created paintings depicting urban scenes that showed how even familiar surroundings could cause the viewer to feel a sense of loneliness. Hopper's Nighthawks is a good example of this. There are four people in the same diner, but they're clearly not together. The bright yellow walls create a dramatic contrast to the darkness outside, emphasizing how people can be in the same space and feel apart. In Hopper's Automat, the feeling of loneliness is even more direct. The yellow lights lead the viewer's eye to the yellow hat of the woman, and the cool shades of the other colors contrast with the warm yellow, emphasizing that she's on her own. body:
밑줄 친 단어의 영영 풀이로 틀린 것은?
Edward Hopper Van Gogh used yellow to express joy, but Edward Hopper’s use of yellow expresses loneliness. Hopper lived in New York City for nearly six decades, and he created paintings depicting urban scenes that showed how even familiar surroundings could cause the viewer to feel a sense of loneliness. Hopper’s Nighthawks is a good example of this. There are four people in the same diner, but they’re clearly not together. The bright yellow walls create a dramatic contrast to the darkness outside, emphasizing how people can be in the same space and feel apart. In Hopper’s Automat, the feeling of loneliness is even more direct. The yellow lights lead the viewer’s eye to the yellow hat of the woman, and the cool shades of the other colors contrast with the warm yellow, emphasizing that she’s on her own.
solution: ④ shade는 ‘색조, 그늘’이라는 뜻으로, 본문에서는 “the cool shades of the other colors”에서 색의 다양한 톤이나 색조를 의미한다. 그러나 제시된 영영 풀이인 “a loud and powerful sound that fills a space”는 ‘크고 강한 소리’ 라는 뜻이므로 shade의 의미와 맞지 않는다. 반면 나머지 선택지는 모두 본문의 의미에 알맞다. ① depict: ‘묘사하다, 나타내다’ ② surroundings: ‘주변 환경’ ③ contrast: ‘대조, 뚜렷한 차이’ ⑤ on one’s own: ‘혼자서, 홀로’ 를 의미한다.
choices: depict: to show or describe something in a picture or story
surroundings: the things and conditions around a person or place
contrast: a noticeable difference between two things
shade: a loud and powerful sound that fills a space
on one’s own: alone; without other people

solution: 작품 Nighthawks에서 카운터 직원이 정면을 응시하고 인물들이 서로 소통하지 않는 묘사는 대도시 속 현대인들이 겪는 단절과 소외감을 시각적으로 극대화하기 위한 장치이다. 따라서 바르게 분석하지 못한 학생은 ④이다.
choices: 서현준: 식당 안의 네 사람은 비록 물리적으로 같은 공간에 있지만, 서로 시선을 나누거나 소통하지 않는 단절된 상태에 있음을 유추할 수 있어.

박찬호: 나란히 앉아 있는 커플 역시 다정해 보이지만, 이들 또한 대도시라는 거대한 공간 속에서 느끼는 익명의 외로움 에서 완전히 벗어나지 못했어.

Van Gogh used yellow to express joy, but Edward Hopper’s use of yellow expresses ⓐloneliness. (B) Hopper’s Nighthawks is a good example of this. There are four people in the same diner, but they’re clearly not together. The bright yellow walls create a dramatic
ⓒcontrast to the darkness outside, emphasizing how people can be in the same space and feel apart. In Hopper’s Automat, the feeling of loneliness is even more
ⓓdirect. The yellow lights lead the viewer’s eye to the yellow hat of the woman, and the cool shades of the other colors contrast with the warm yellow,

양준 선생님의 지시: 정민아, 접속사 대신 관계대명사의 계속 적 용법을 활용해보렴. 그리고 동사의 목적격보어가 알맞은 형식으로 쓰였는지도 검토해 봐.
→ 4회차 실전 모의고사
answer: Hopper lived in New York City for nearly six decades, in which he created paintings depicting urban scenes that showed how even familiar surroundings could cause the viewer to feel a sense of loneliness.
solution: 접속사 and 대신 의미를 연결할 수 있는 관계대명사 in which를 사용했으며, cause는 목적격보어로 to부정사를 취하므로, feeling은 to feel로 고쳐야 한다.

body:
다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
We take it for granted that we should smile for the camera. But a century ago, stone-faced photos were the norm. The smiles we flash for the camera today are about ten times bigger than the smiles photographed 100 years ago. A team of computer scientists analyzed more than 37,000 U.S. high school yearbook portraits from 1905 to 2013. They measured each person's smile by comparing the shape of their mouths. In the 1910s, lip angles were almost zero, meaning mouths were mostly flat. But in the post-World War II era, people opened their mouths in their yearbook photos. Why did this happen? 4회차 실전 모의고사 Manners of the past demanded that the mouth be carefully controlled, and a small mouth was considered beautiful. Big smiles were viewed as silly or mean. That's why a serious expression was common in most painted portraits, both in the East and West. Even after the invention of photography, the tradition continued.
The spread of cameras and camera companies' advertising campaigns changed the trend. Early photographers were not very good at getting people to relax in front of the camera, so they were not satisfied with their photos. To popularize cameras, the companies tried to change this by launching advertising campaigns that _____ . Companies wanted to show customers that the camera was a tool for capturing happy moments. They also found that happy images helped their sales, so they began using smiling models in their advertisements. Official images followed suit, and by the 1950s, presidents were smiling in their portraits.
solution: ① 빈칸이 포함된 문장은 카메라를 대중화하기 위해 회사들이 광고 캠페인을 시작했다는 내용이며, 바로 다음 문장에서 'Companies wanted to show customers that the camera was a tool for capturing happy moments'라고 하여 사진을 축제·행복한 순간과 연결지으려 했음을 밝히고 있다. 따라서 빈칸에는 광고 캠페인이 사진 촬영을 축하·기념과 연결시켰다는 내용이 와야 한다. 따라서 'associated photography with celebration'이 흐름상 가장 자연스럽다.
choices: associated photography with celebration
highlighted the technical skills of photographers
discouraged people from taking serious portraits
promoted the beauty of a small and controlled mouth
introduced smiling models to painted portrait traditions 유형보충독해1

body:
밑줄 친 단어의 영영 풀이로 맞는 것은?
The Story of Smiling Selfies We take it for granted that we should smile for the camera. But a century ago, stone-faced photos were the norm. The smiles we flash for the camera today are about ten times bigger than the smiles photographed 100 years ago. A team of computer scientists analyzed more than 37,000 U.S. high school yearbook portraits from 1905 to 2013. They measured each person’s smile by comparing the shape of their mouths. In the 1910s, lip angles were almost zero, meaning mouths were mostly flat. But in the post-World War II era, people opened their mouths in their yearbook photos. Why did this happen? Manners of the past demanded that the mouth be carefully controlled, and a small mouth was considered beautiful. Big smiles were viewed as silly or mean. That’s why a serious expression was common in most painted portraits, both in the East and West. Even after the invention of photography, the tradition continued. The spread of cameras and camera companies’ advertising campaigns changed the trend. Early photographers were not very good at getting people to relax in front of the camera, so they were not satisfied with their photos. To popularize cameras, the companies tried to change this by launching advertising campaigns that associated photography with celebration. Companies wanted to show customers that the camera was a tool for capturing happy moments. They also found that happy images helped their sales, so they began using smiling models in their advertisements. Official images followed suit, and by the 1950s, presidents were smiling in their portraits.
solution: ② analyze는 ‘분석하다, 자세히 조사하다’라는 뜻으로, 본문에서는 컴퓨터 과학자들이 37,000장이 넘는 졸업사진을 조사하고 미소의 형태를 비교했다는 내용에서 사용되었다. 따라서 “to study something carefully in order to understand it”이라는 영영 풀이가 알맞다. 반면 나머지 선택지는 어휘의 의미와 맞지 않는다. ① stone-faced는 ‘무표정한, 굳은 표정의’라는 뜻인데, 제시된 풀이는 ‘신나거나 행복한 표정의’라는 의미이므로 틀리다. ③ portrait는 ‘초상화, 인물 사진’인데, 제시된 풀이는 풍경화를 의미하므로 틀리다. ④ popularize는 ‘널리 알리다, 대중화하다’라는 뜻인데, 제시된 풀이는 ‘덜 알려지게 하다’이므로 반대 의미이다. ⑤ advertisement는 ‘광고’라는 뜻인데, 제시된 풀이는 ‘개인 편지’의 의미이므로 틀리다.
choices: stone-faced: showing strong excitement or happiness on the face
analyze: to study something carefully in order to understand it
portrait: a picture of a natural place such as mountains or forests
popularize: to make something less known to people
advertisement: a private letter sent from one person to another 유형보충독해1

solution: ③ 사진 발명 이후에도 진지한 표정의 전통이 계속되었다고 명시되어 있으므로, 사진 기술이 발명 당시부터 회화와 다른 표정을 담아냈다는 내용은 추론할 수 없다. ① 작은 입과 진지한 표정이 과거의 기준이었다가 이후 미소가 표준이 되었다는 변화로 보아, 표정에 대한 사회적 기준이 시대에 따라 달라질 수 있음을 추론할 수 있다. ② 카메라 회사의 광고가 사람들의 표정(자기표현 방식)을 미소로 바꾸는 데 영향을 미쳤다는 내용으로 보아 추론할 수 있다. ④ 광고 속 미소가 결국 대통령의 공식 초상에도 반영되었다는 내용으로 보아, 대중적 변화가 공적 영역에도 영향을 줄 수 있음을 추론할 수 있다. ⑤ 행복한 이미지가 판매에 도움이 되었다는 내용으로 보아, 긍정적 감정과 제품을 연결하는 전략이 소비자 행동에 영향을 줄 수 있음을 추론할 수 있다.
choices: 표정에 대한 사회적 기준은 시대에 따라 달라질 수 있다.
기업의 마케팅 전략은 사람들의 자기표현 방식에 영향을 줄 수 있다.

대중적 이미지에서 나타난 변화는 공적인 영역의 이미지에 도 영향을 줄 수 있다.
제품과 긍정적 감정을 연결하는 전략은 소비자의 구매 행동 에 영향을 줄 수 있다. 유형보충독해1

다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 할 때, 빈칸 (A),
(B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
Manners of the past demanded that the mouth be carefully controlled, and a small mouth was considered beautiful. Big smiles were viewed as silly or mean. That’s why a serious expression was common in most painted portraits, both in the East and West. Even after the invention of photography, the tradition continued. The spread of cameras and camera companies’ advertising campaigns changed the trend. Early photographers were not very good at getting people to relax in front of the camera, so they were not satisfied with their photos. To popularize cameras, the companies tried to change this by launching advertising campaigns that associated photography with celebration. Companies wanted to show customers that the camera was a tool for capturing happy moments. They also found that happy images helped their sales, so they began using smiling models in their advertisements. Official images followed suit, and by the 1950s, presidents were smiling in their portraits. Portraits once favored (A) _____ expressions, but camera companies' advertising campaigns, which linked photography with happiness, gradually made (B) _____ expressions the new standard.
solution: 요약문은 초상화가 한때 (A) '진지한(serious)' 표정을 선호했으나, 사진을 행복과 연결시킨 카메라 회사들의 광고 캠페인이 점차 (B) '미소 짓는(smiling)' 표정을 새로운 표준으로 만들었다는 것을 설명한다. (A) 본문에서 'a serious expression was common in most painted portraits(대부분의 초상화에서 진지한 표정이 흔했다)'라고 했으므로, '진지한(serious)'이라는 표현이 들어가야 알맞다. (B) 본문에서 카메라 회사들이 사진을 행복과 연관 짓는 광고 캠페인을 통해 미소 짓는 모델을 광고에 사용하기 시작했고, 결국 1950년대에는 대통령들도 초상화에서 미소를 짓게 되었다고 했으므로, '미소 짓는(smiling)'이라는 표현이 들어가야 알맞다. 따라서, 정답은 ④ serious - smiling 이 가장 알맞다.
choices: relaxed - serious
casual - formal
serious - formal
serious - smiling
formal - relaxed

밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 어색한 것을 찾아 기호를 적고 옳게 고쳐 쓰시오.

Colorful Stories of Art Many artists are famous for their particular use of color. While some artists mix interesting and unique colors, other artists use primary colors ⓐto express strong emotions. As we walk through our newest exhibition, Colorful Stories of Art, we will explore the use of the three primary colors—yellow, blue, and red—and find out how they were a source of inspiration. Open your eyes, listen to the stories, and try to feel the emotions that the colors show. Vincent van Gogh The first artist is Vincent van Gogh. According to research, the French city of Arles, ⓑwhich van Gogh spent his later years, had exceptionally bright and intense sunlight. Van Gogh expressed the sunlight, energy, and the joy of life he felt there through bright yellow colors. During his short life of 37 years, he created more than 900 paintings, around 300 of which feature mostly yellow. The series of paintings called Sunflowers ⓒincludes some of his most recognizable works. Some have said that his preference for yellow in his artwork was due to a medical condition that forced him ⓓseeing mainly yellow. A kangaroo's tail, ⓐthat is made up of over twenty vertebrae, acts as a powerful muscle for balance and movement. The tail works almost like a fifth leg ⓑso that the kangaroo can hop, turn, and even fight without losing stability. When a kangaroo stands still, its tail ⓒsupports most of its body weight while the legs rest. During a fight, a kangaroo often begins ⓓkicking its opponent with both hind legs while balancing on its tail. Before hopping away, the kangaroo tucks its front legs close to its chest to protect ⓔthem from injury. *vertebrae: 척추뼈
solution: ①ⓐ이 정답이다. 'A kangaroo's tail, that is made up of over twenty vertebrae'에서 콤마 뒤의 계속적 용법 관계대명사로는 'that'을 쓸 수 없으므로 'which'로 고쳐야 한다. ⓑ 'so that'은 뒤에 완전한 절이 이어져 목적이나 결과를 나타내는 접속사로 올바르다. ⓒ 주어 'its tail'이 단수이므로 단수동사 'supports'가 알맞다. ⓓ 'begin + -ing' 구조에서 'kicking'이 올바르게 쓰였다. ⓔ 'them'은 앞의 복수명사 'front legs'를 가리키는 대명사로 적절하다.

A lot of scholars have this view because ⓒit is easier to separate art from science than to combine them. ⓔis needed for interdisciplinary learning to thrive.

Thus, this experiment shows that most of us seem to (B)
[know / be known] how to hide our nerves to some extent. Whether or not we're aware that the way we move reveals our nervousness, we control it (C)[automatic / automatically]. 실전 학습
solution: (A) ask + 목적어 + to부정사 구조이므로 to perform이 적절하다. (B) seem to + 동사원형 구조이며, 문맥상 ‘우리가 스스로 아는 것’이라는 능동의 의미이므로 know가 적절하다. be known은 ‘알려지다’라는 수동의 의미가 되어 문맥에 맞지 않는다. (C) 동사 control을 수식해야 하므로 부사 automatically가 적절하다. 형용사 automatic은 동사를 수식할 수 없다.

body:

Fast food consumption has had positive influences on the way people manage their busy schedules and save time. However, although fast food seems to make life more convenient, it is actually creating more health risks. The more often people eat fast food, the less balanced nutrition they get. Many doctors now believe that poor nutrition can lead to a number of physical problems. In fact, a recent study showed that fast food increases blood sugar levels, that explains why people who eat fast food regularly experience significant levels of obesity, diabetes, and other health issues.
→
solution: 콤마 뒤에서 앞에 나온 절 전체를 선행사로 받아 추가 설명을 덧붙이는 비제한적 관계대명사 자리에는 that을 쓸 수 없으므로 which로 고쳐야 한다. 'increases blood sugar levels, that explains why'의 that을 which로 바꿔야 한다. 비상(홍) 3과 문법 정복 실전
source: 영어플랫 · 비상(홍) 공통영어2 3과 문법 정복 실전

body:
어법상 틀린 것을 모두 골라 기호를 쓰고 바르게 고치시오.
ⓐDid you see the boy and his rabbit that were playing in the garden?
ⓑThis is all that matters to me now.
ⓒChoose that you feel is best for you.
ⓓShe is the only friend that supported me.
ⓔThe tool with that he built the table is gone.
→
→
answer: ⓒ that → what, ⓔ with that → with which
solution: ⓒ은 선행사 없이 '~하는 것'이라는 의미로 관계대명사 that을 명사절처럼 쓴 오류로, that을 what으로 고쳐야 한다. (Choose what you feel is best for you.) ⓔ는 관계대명사 that이 전치사 바로 뒤에 올 수 없으므로 with that을 with which로 고쳐야 한다. (The tool with which he built the table is gone.) ⓐ은 선행사가 사람(boy)과 동물(rabbit)이 함께 있을 때 관계대명사 that을 쓰는 것이 자연스러우므로 옳다. ⓑ는 all이 선행사일 때 관계대명사 that을 쓰는 것이 적절하므로 옳다. ⓓ는 the only가 선행사를 수식할 때 관계대명사 that을 쓰는 것이 자연스러우므로 옳다.

solution: 정답은 ①이다. 지각동사 heard는 목적어와 목적격보어가 능동관계일 때 현재분사(singing)를 목적격보어로 쓴다. leave는 목적어와 목적격보어가 수동관계일 때 과거분사 (locked)를 목적격보어로 쓴다. 따라서 singing - locked가 정답이다. ② to sing은 지각동사의 목적격보어로 부정사를 쓸 수 없어 틀렸고, lock은 목적어(the office)와 수동관계이므로 과거분사가 와야 한다. ③ to sing은 지각동사의 목적격보어로 부정사를 쓸 수 없고, locking은 the office와 능동관계가 아니라 수동관계이므로 틀렸다. ④ singing은 맞지만 lock은 원형으로 the office와 수동관계를 나타낼 수 없어 틀렸다. ⑤ sang은 동사의 과거형이므로 목적격보어로 쓸 수 없어 틀렸다.

to sing - lock
to sing - locking _____
singing - lock
sang - locked

A protein in the venom of cone snails could help chronic pain patients ⓐmanaged their symptoms without addictive drugs. Chronic pain occurs when nerve cells continue sending pain signals to the brain long after an injury has healed. The protein in snail venom makes these nerve cells
ⓑstopping the signals immediately, so patients can continue ⓒfunction normally in daily life. Researchers think the same protein may be able to relieve pain in humans without causing dependence. Fortunately the protein would
ⓓturned into a simple pill, and patients would not be required ⓔreceiving painful injections. * venom 독 / chronic 만성의
solution: ③ continue는 to부정사나 동명사를 목적어로 취하므로 'function'은 'to function' 또는 'functioning'으로 고쳐야 한다. 그런데 이를 과거형 'functioned'로 잘못 고쳤으므로 어법상 틀린 수정이다. ① 'help + 목적어 + 동사원형' 구조이므로 'managed'는 'manage'로 고치는 것이 옳다. ② 'make + 목적어 + 동사원형' 구조이므로 'stopping'은 'stop'으로 고치는 것이 옳다. ④ 조동사 would 뒤에는 동사원형이 와야 하므로 수동태 'be turned'로 고치는 것이 옳다. ⑤ 'be required + to부정사' 구조이므로 'receiving'은 'to receive'로 고치는 것이 옳다.

body:

body:
밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중 어법상 맞는 것을 두 개 고르면?
Remember that patience is essential when resolving a conflict between siblings. If your apology is not accepted right away, thank your brother for listening to you and ⓐleft the door open for future reconciliation. Keep in mind ⓑthat just because a sibling accepts your apology does not mean he has fully forgiven you. It can take time, maybe a long time, before the ⓒhurting sibling can completely trust you again. There is
ⓓlittle you can do to speed up this process. If the relationship truly matters to you, it is worth giving him the time and space needed to heal. Do not expect him ⓔgo back to normal immediately.
① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ
solution: 정답은 ②, ④이다. ②는 the fact에 해당하는 명사절을 이끄는 접속사 that으로 올바르게 쓰였다. ④는 you can do가 불가산적 개념이므로 little이 올바르게 쓰였다. ①은 'thank ~ for listening ... and leaving ...'처럼 동명사로 병렬되어야 하는데 과거형 left가 쓰여 병렬 구조가 깨져 어법상 틀리다. ③은 '상처받은 형제'라는 의미이므로 과거분사 hurt가 되어야 하는데 현재분사 hurting이 쓰여 어법상 틀리다. ⑤는 'expect + 목적어 + to부정사' 구조가 되어야 하므로 go 앞에 to가 필요한데 빠져 있어 어법상 틀리다.

(left) 구조가 올바르게 쓰였으므로 옳다. ⑤ 전치사 instead of, despite 뒤에 각각 동명사 complaining, not being able to+동사원형 구조가 올바르게 쓰였으므로 옳다. ② 감정을 느끼는 주체 team을 수식하므로 confused(감정을 느끼는)가 되어야 하며, confusing(감정을 일으키는)은 틀렸다. ④ heard(지각동사) 뒤 목적격 보어로 to complain이 아니라 원형부정사나 현재분사인 complain 또는 complaining이 와야 하므로 틀렸다.

body:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것을 2개 고르면?
Money was once viewed merely as a tool for barter in ancient marketplaces. As barter systems
ⓐdeclined in early civilizations, currency began to be used for trade. Merchants and traders believed ⓑthat coins were more reliable than goods, especially when trading across long distances. The powerful did all they could to control minting, perhaps except for a small transaction, ⓒit was regarded as harmless. Later, as paper money and banknotes ⓓreplacing metal coins across kingdoms, currency in modern society was viewed as a symbol of trust. Their innovations influenced economists such as Adam Smith, whose theories ⓔwere praised for explaining the value of money.
① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ 실전 학습 교과서 문법 정복
solution: ③ⓒ과 ④ⓓ가 어법상 틀리다. ⓒ은 콤마로 연결되어 앞의 명사 a small transaction를 수식하는 관계사절이 와야 하므로, 인칭대명사 it이 아니라 관계대명사 which를 써야 한다 (it → which). ⓓ는 'as+주어+동사'로 이루어진 부사절이므로 현재분사 replacing이 아니라 과거시제 동사 replaced가 와야 한다 (replacing → replaced). ⓐ의 declined는 주어 systems와 수가 일치하는 올바른 과거시제 동사이다. ⓑ의 that은 believed의 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이끄는 접속사로 올바르게 쓰였다. ⓔ의 were praised는 문맥상 적절한 수동태 과거시제이다.
source: 영어플랫 · 비상(홍) 공통영어2 3과 문법 정복 실전

body:
다음 글 (A), (B)의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 적절한 것끼리 짝지어진 것은?
(A) A Yale study by physiologist Mark Diaz found
ⓐthat once a person consuming more than 400 milligrams of caffeine daily, the risk of irregular heartbeat increased slightly. He analyzed health records of over 250,000 adults in the National Cardiac Health Survey, a long-term study conducted by the Yale School of Medicine, and discovered that cardiac risk rises with caffeine intake — but not below 300 milligrams per day. What is the significance of 300 milligrams? It's not an arbitrary threshold. It appears ⓑto be the amount deemed “moderate” for maintaining stable heart function. And the researchers found that ⓒhigh caffeine intake did not in itself cause arrhythmia, but made people felt more anxious about symptoms they already experienced. In other words, that old caution “too much caffeine harms the heart” turns out to be true.
(B) Background music in the office has notable effects on mood and the ability to type accurately. Thus, it is not surprising ⓓthat constant exposure to loud background music is related to employees' typing accuracy, particularly in its negative effects on error rates and speed. Some researchers found that, ⓔwhen office playlists were adjusted to lower volumes, the employees made fewer typing mistakes and completed tasks more quickly, and their performance on accuracy tests improved. Research with call center workers suggests similar findings. On accuracy and speed tests,
ⓕemployees working in loud open-plan offices or workspaces consistently perform below that in quieter offices.
solution: 정답은 ②이다. ⓑ, ⓓ, ⓔ가 어법상 적절하다. ⓐ once가 이끄는 부사절의 주어(a person) 뒤에는 본동사가 와야 하므로, 준동사 consuming을 과거동사인 consumed(또는 consumes)로 고쳐야 한다. ⓒ 'made people felt'는 'made people feel'로 고쳐야 한다. made는 사역동사이므로 목적격 보어로 동사원형이 와야 한다. ⓑ 'appear to be + 명사(구)'는 '~인 것처럼 보이다'라는 뜻으로 적절하게 쓰였다. ⓓ 'it is not surprising that + 완전한 문장'은 가주어- 진주어 구문으로 적절하게 쓰였다. ⓔ 'when + 주어 + were + p.p.'는 시간의 부사절에서 수동태가 적절하게 쓰였다. ⓕ 'perform below that'은 'perform below those'로 고쳐야 한다. that은 앞에 나온 복수명사(employees)의 수행 능력을 대신하므로 those로 써야 한다.
source: 영어플랫 · 비상(홍) 공통영어2 3과 문법 정복 실전

body:
다음 중, 어법상 틀린 것끼리 짝지은 것은?
Dr. Nora Wells and James Park, experts on social media use, recognized that platforms and screen-time trackers ⓐhave been frequently used to help isolated teenagers stay connected with friends, and encourage people who feel lonely to reach out more often. ⓑBut they were convinced the apps could also encourage anxious users compare themselves constantly to others. Wells explained that ⓒscrolling through endless feeds create a false sense of connection.
ⓓShe noted that comparing one's life to curated posts often triggers deep dissatisfaction, which can worsen a person's mental state over time. He recently experienced a severe anxiety episode
ⓔbecause he refused to put down his phone at night, ⓕinstead scrolled for hours without any real rest. Park has struggled with social media dependence, and now sets strict limits on his screen time.
solution: 정답은 ⑤(ⓑⓒⓕ)이다. ⓑ는 'encourage + 목적어 + to부정사' 구조가 되어야 하므로 'encourage anxious users compare'는 'encourage anxious users to compare'로 고쳐야 한다. ⓒ는 동명사구 주어(scrolling through endless feeds)는 단수로 취급하므로 'create'는 'creates'가 되어야 한다. ⓕ는 앞의 주절과 별개의 동작을 연결하면서 등위접속사 없이 콤마로 이어졌으므로 and를 넣어야 한다. ⓐ, ⓓ, ⓔ는 각각 to부정사와 원형부정사의 올바른 병렬 구조, 동명사구 주어와 단수 동사의 일치, because절의 올바른 구조가 모두 어법상 옳다. 비상(홍) 3과 문법 정복 실전
source: 영어플랫 · 비상(홍) 공통영어2 3과 문법 정복 실전
choices: ⓑ, ⓒ, ⓕ 실전 학습 교과서 문법 정복

body:
다음 중, 어법상 옳은 문장의 개수는?
ⓐThe town festival is taken place in the central square every summer, attracting visitors from neighboring villages.
ⓑJust like the siblings in the Bronte's novel, Claire and Noah will support each other more when their bond will be challenged by distance.
ⓒIn 1969, the astronaut experienced a technical malfunction during the mission and barely survived from lose consciousness for several minutes.
ⓓStudying abroad not only broadens your perspective, but it can also help you gain independence at a young age.

We take it for granted that we should smile for the camera. But a century ago, stone-faced photos were the norm. The smiles we flash for the camera today are about ten times ⓐbiggest than the smiles photographed 100 years ago. A team of computer scientists analyzed more than 37,000 U.S. high school yearbook portraits from 1905 to 2013. They measured each person's smile ⓑby compare the shape of their mouths. In the 1910s, lip angles were almost zero, meaning mouths were mostly flat. But in the post-World War II era, people opened their mouths in their yearbook photos. Why did this happen? Manners of the past demanded that the mouth
ⓒbe carefully controlled, and a small mouth was considered beautiful. Big smiles were viewed as silly or mean. That's why a serious expression was common in most painted portraits, both in the East and West. Even after the invention of photography, the tradition continued. 실전 학습 The spread of cameras and camera companies' advertising campaigns changed the trend. Early photographers were not very good at getting people ⓓto relaxing in front of the camera, so they were not satisfied with their photos. To popularize cameras, the companies tried to change this by launching advertising campaigns that associated photography with celebration.
Companies wanted to show customers that the camera was a tool for capturing happy moments. They also found that happy images helped their sales, so they began ⓔused smiling models in their advertisements. Official images followed suit, and by the 1950s, presidents were smiling in their portraits.
solution: ③이 정답이다. ③ 'demanded that the mouth be carefully controlled'에서 동사 demand는 당위적 의미를 나타내어 that절에 '(should +) 동사원형'을 요구하는 당위적 가정법을 취한다. 따라서 be가 원형동사로 올바르게 쓰였다. ① biggest → bigger 배수 표현(ten times)과 함께 두 대상을 비교할 때는 반드시 비교급을 사용해야 한다. 최상급 biggest는 세 개 이상을 비교할 때 쓰이므로 비교급 bigger로 고쳐야 한다. ② by compare → by comparing 전치사 by 뒤에는 동사원형이 아닌 동명사(v-ing)가 와야 한다. 따라서 compare를 comparing으로 고쳐야 한다. ④ to relaxing → to relax get + 목적어 + to부정사 구조에서 목적격보어로는 'to + 동사원형'이 와야 한다. to 뒤에 동명사 relaxing을 쓸 수 없으므로 to relax로 고쳐야 한다. ⑤ used → using began 뒤에는 동명사(v-ing) 또는 to부정사가 목적어로 올 수 있지만, 과거분사 used는 목적어 자리에 올 수 없다. 따라서 using으로 고쳐야 한다. 비상(홍) 3과 문법 정복 실전

body:
밑줄 친 부분 중 어법 상 어색한 것을 모두 찾아 기호를 적고 옳게 고쳐 쓰시오.
Many artists are famous for their particular use of color. While some artists mix interesting and
ⓐunique colors, other artists use primary colors to express strong emotions. As we walk through our newest exhibition, Colorful Stories of Art, we will explore the use of the three primary colors— yellow, blue, and red—and find out ⓑwhat they were a source of inspiration. Open your eyes, listen to the stories, and try to feel the emotions that the colors show. Vincent van Gogh The first artist is Vincent van Gogh. According to research, the French city of Arles, where van Gogh spent his later years, had exceptionally bright and intense sunlight. Van Gogh expressed the sunlight, energy, and the joy of life he felt there through bright yellow colors. During his short life of 37 years, he created more than 900 paintings, around 300 ⓒof which feature mostly yellow. The series of paintings called Sunflowers includes some of his most recognizable works. Some have said that his preference for yellow in his artwork was due to a medical condition that forced him to see mainly yellow. While this may be true, we can also see his use of blue, orange, and other colors, and these combinations of colors serve to emphasize his joy ⓓconveying. Edward Hopper Van Gogh used yellow to express joy, but Edward Hopper's use of yellow expresses loneliness. Hopper lived in New York City for nearly six decades, and he created paintings ⓔdepicting urban scenes that showed how even familiar surroundings could cause the viewer to feel a sense of loneliness. Hopper's Nighthawks is a good example of this. There are four people in the same diner, but they're clearly not together. The bright yellow walls create a dramatic contrast to the darkness outside, emphasizing how people can be in the same space and feel apart. In Hopper's Automat, the feeling of loneliness is even more direct. The yellow lights lead the viewer's eye to the yellow hat of the woman, and the cool shades of the other colors contrast with own. 실전 학습 , _____ → , _____ →
solution: ⓑ what → how "find out" 뒤에 이어지는 절 "they were a source of inspiration"은 주어(they)와 동사(were), 보어(a source of inspiration)를 모두 갖춘 완전한 문장 구조이다. 따라서 명사절을 이끄는 접속사로 '어떻게 ~였는지'의 의미를 나타내는 how가 적절하다. what은 명사절 안에서 주어나 목적어 역할을 해야 하는데, 뒤 절이 이미 완전하므로 what은 올 수 없다. ⓓ conveying → being conveyed "his joy"는 색깔들의 조합에 의해 '전달되는' 대상이므로 수동의 의미를 나타내야 한다. 따라서 능동형 현재분사 conveying이 아니라 수동의 의미를 가진 being conveyed가 올바르다. ⓐ "unique"는 앞의 형용사 "interesting"과 병렬 구조를 이루며 명사 "colors"를 수식하는 형용사로 올바르게 쓰였다. ⓒ "of which"는 선행사 "900 paintings" 중 일부인 "300"을 나타내는 [수사 + of which] 구조의 관계대명사구로 올바르게 쓰였다. ⓔ "depicting"은 앞의 명사 "paintings"를 수식하는 현재분사로, paintings가 능동적으로 도시 장면을 묘사하는 주체이므로 올바르게 쓰였다.
source: 영어플랫 · 비상(홍) 공통영어2 3과 문법 정복 실전

body:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 옳은 것은?
Our last color is red, which is often associated with life and energy. R.C. Gorman, ⓐknowing as the Picasso of Native American art, may have felt the same way when he created Navajo Velvet. The painting depicts a woman sitting on the ground, deep in thought. Her figure in a red dress resembles a huge mountain against the background of the deep, starry blue night,
ⓑsuggested the relationship between her and nature. Sometimes red is used to express the beauty of nature. Claude Monet's Autumn Effect at Argenteuil shows ⓒhow the artist celebrated beautiful autumn moments. The bright reds in the painting symbolize the amazing and transformative power of nature. The painting captures the dramatic moment when the forest
ⓓturned bright red and is reflected on the surface of the river. Color is powerful because it stimulates such an emotional response in us. Artists use the same color to express various feelings, so the way we interpret the artwork can be various too. Open your eyes and let the emotions of the artwork
ⓔto come to you. You may love it or you may hate it, but art will always take you to a place beyond everyday life.
solution: ③이 정답이다. ③ Claude Monet's Autumn Effect at Argenteuil shows how the artist celebrated beautiful autumn moments.에서 'shows'의 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이끄는 접속사로 how가 쓰였다. 'how + 주어 + 동사'의 간접의문문 구조로, 동사 shows의 목적어절을 올바르게 이끌고 있어 어법상 옳다. 학생들이 what이나 that으로 혼동하기 쉽지만, '어떻게 화가가 아름다운 가을의 순간들을 기렸는지'라는 방법의 의미로 how가 적절하다. ① knowing as → known as R.C. Gorman은 '피카소로 알려진' 대상이므로 수동의 의미를 나타내야 한다. 주어(R.C. Gorman)와 분사의 관계가 수동(~ 로 알려진)이므로 현재분사 knowing이 아닌 과거분사 known을 써야 한다. 'be known as'의 수동 관계에서 비롯된 과거분사구문이어야 하므로 knowing as를 known as로 고쳐야 한다. ② suggested → suggesting 문장의 주어인 'Her figure in a red dress'가 능동적으로 '암시하는' 행위를 하는 것이므로 능동의 분사구문이 필요하다. 과거분사 suggested는 수동의 의미(~되어진)를 나타내므로 문맥과 맞지 않는다. 능동의 현재분사 suggesting으로 고쳐야 한다. ④ turned → turns 이 문장은 그림이 묘사하는 내용을 현재시제로 서술하는 문맥이다. 같은 절 내 'is reflected'가 현재시제로 쓰여 있고, 앞 문장들도 현재시제로 일관되게 서술하고 있으므로, when절의 동사도 현재시제 turns로 써야 한다. 과거시제 turned는 이 문맥에서 어법상 적절하지 않다. ⑤ to come → come 사역동사 let은 목적격 보어로 동사원형(원형부정사)을 취한다. 'let + 목적어 + 동사원형'의 구조이므로, to come이 아닌 원형부정사 come을 써야 한다. 비상(홍) 3과 문법 정복 실전

The color blue can produce a calming effect. Even during his days in Paris and New York, Kim Whanki never ⓐforgot his Korean identity. The blue sky and blue seas reminded him of Sinan, his home in Korea, which inspired him to create paintings filled with various shades of blue. His use of blue was an expression of ⓑhow much he missed the place he grew up in. In Tranquility 5- IV-73 #310, the waves of deep blue and light blue dots ⓒbring up images of the sea or the sky. Kim Whanki said that he painted each dot as he thought of friends and loved ones from home. On the other hand, Henri Matisse's blue speaks of freedom. Polynesia, the Sky and Polynesia, the Sea are two Matisse works that have an interesting similarity. In his later years, Matisse had cancer surgery, which left him ⓓunable to stand and paint in front of an easel. Instead of painting, he created artwork by gluing paper cut- outs and then painting details. Although his physical difficulties prevented him from ⓔto do many things, he still remembered the freedom he experienced while swimming in the Tahitian sea, looking through the salt water down to the sea floor and up towards the sky.

"prevented him from to do"는 어법상 틀리며, "prevented him from doing"으로 고쳐야 한다. 따라서 ⑤가 정답이다. ① 문맥상 김환기가 한국인의 정체성을 '잊지 않았다'는 과거 사실을 나타내므로, 과거시제 동사 forgot이 올바르게 쓰였다. ② 전치사 of의 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이끄는 표현으로, '얼마나 많이 그리워했는지'라는 의미의 간접의문문이다. how much가 올바르게 쓰였다. ③ 문장의 주어는 "the waves of deep blue and light blue dots"로 복수 명사이므로, 복수형 동사 bring이 올바르게 쓰였다. ④ `leave + 목적어 + 형용사 보어` 구문으로, 수술 후 마티스가 이젤 앞에 서서 그림을 그릴 수 없는 상태가 되었다는 의미이다. 형용사 unable이 목적격 보어로 올바르게 쓰였다.

Van Gogh used yellow to express joy, but Edward Hopper's use of yellow expresses loneliness. Hopper lived in New York City for nearly six decades, and he created paintings ⓐdepicting urban scenes ⓑwho showed ⓒhow even familiar surroundings could cause the viewer to feel a sense of loneliness. Hopper's Nighthawks is a good example of this. There are four people in the same diner, but they're clearly not together. The bright yellow walls create a dramatic contrast to the darkness outside, ⓓemphasizing how people can be in the same space and feel apart. In Hopper's Automat, the feeling of loneliness is even more direct. The yellow lights ⓔlead the viewer's eye to the yellow hat of the woman, and the cool shades of the other colors contrast with the warm yellow, emphasizing that she's on her own.
solution: ② who showed → that showed (또는 which showed) 선행사인 'urban scenes'는 사물이므로 사람을 받는 주격 관계대명사 who를 쓸 수 없다. 사물 선행사에는 관계대명사 that 또는 which를 써야 한다. 따라서 ③이 정답이다. ① 'he created paintings depicting urban scenes'에서 depicting은 paintings를 후치 수식하는 현재분사이다. paintings가 urban scenes를 '묘사하는' 능동 관계이므로 현재분사 depicting이 올바르게 쓰였다. ③ 'showed how even familiar surroundings could cause …'에서 how는 showed의 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이끄는 접속사로 올바르게 쓰였다. ④ 'emphasizing how people can be in the same space and feel apart'에서 emphasizing은 앞 절 전체 내용을 부연하는 분사구문으로, 주어인 The bright yellow walls가 능동적으로 강조하는 주체이므로 현재분사 emphasizing이 올바르게 쓰였다. ⑤ 'The yellow lights lead the viewer's eye'에서 주어 The yellow lights는 복수 명사이므로 동사원형 lead가 올바르게 쓰였다.

밑줄 친 부분 중 어법 상 어색한 것을 모두 찾아 기호를 적고 옳게 고쳐 쓰시오.
The first artist is Vincent van Gogh. According to research, the French city of Arles, ⓐwhere van Gogh spent his later years, had exceptionally bright and intense sunlight. Van Gogh expressed the sunlight, energy, and the joy of life he
ⓑfeeling there through bright yellow colors. During his short life of 37 years, he created more than 900 paintings, around 300 ⓒof which feature mostly yellow. The series of paintings
ⓓcalling Sunflowers includes some of his most recognizable works. Some have said that his preference for yellow in his artwork was due to a medical condition that forced him to see mainly yellow. While this may be true, we can also see his use of blue, orange, and other colors, and these combinations of colors serve ⓔto emphasize his joy being conveyed. , _____ → , _____ →
solution: ⓑ feeling → felt 관계대명사가 생략된 목적격 관계절 'he there'에서 동사가 필요하다. 문맥상 '그가 그곳에서 느꼈던 삶의 기쁨'이라는 의미이므로, 분사형 feeling이 아니라 과거 시제 동사 felt가 와야 한다. feeling은 이 자리에서 관계절의 정동사 역할을 할 수 없다. ⓓ calling → called 'The series of paintings'를 뒤에서 수식하는 분사구이다. 'Sunflowers'라는 이름으로 불리는 것은 paintings이므로, paintings와 call의 관계는 수동(paintings are called Sunflowers)이다. 따라서 능동의 현재분사 calling이 아니라 수동의 과거분사 called가 와야 한다. ⓐ 'the French city of Arles'를 선행사로 하는 관계절에서 '반 고흐가 만년을 보낸 장소'라는 의미이므로, 장소를 나타내는 관계부사 where가 올바르게 쓰였다. ⓒ 'around 300 of which feature mostly yellow'는 「of which + 주어 + 동사」 구조의 관계절로, 선행사 '900 paintings' 중 300점을 가리킨다. 주어가 복수(300)이므로 동사 feature(복수 일치)도 올바르게 쓰였다. ⓔ 'serve to-부정사' 구조는 '~하는 역할을 하다'라는 의미의 관용 표현으로, to emphasize가 올바르게 쓰였다.

[sitting / seating] on the ground, deep in thought. Her figure in a red dress resembles a huge mountain against the background of the deep, starry blue night, (C) [suggesting / suggested] the relationship between her and nature. Sometimes red is used to (D) [express / expressing] the beauty of nature. Claude Monet's Autumn Effect at Argenteuil shows how the artist celebrated beautiful autumn moments. The bright reds in the painting (E) [symbolize / symbolizes] the amazing and transformative power of nature. The painting captures the dramatic moment when the forest turns bright red and is reflected on the surface of the river.

Colorful Stories of Art Many artists are famous for their particular use of color. While some artists mix interesting and ⓐunique colors, other artists use primary colors to express strong emotions. As we walk through our newest exhibition, Colorful Stories of Art, we will explore the use of the three primary colors—yellow, blue, and red—and find out how they were a source of ⓑdiscouragement. Open your eyes, listen to the stories, and try to feel the emotions that the colors show. Vincent van Gogh The first artist is Vincent van Gogh. According to research, the French city of Arles, where van Gogh spent his later years, had exceptionally bright and ⓒintense sunlight. Van Gogh expressed the sunlight, energy, and the joy of life he felt there through bright yellow colors. During his short life of 37 years, he created more than 900 paintings, around 300 of which feature mostly yellow. The series of paintings called Sunflowers includes some of his most
ⓓrecognizable works. Some have said that his preference for yellow in his artwork was due to a medical condition that forced him to see mainly yellow. While this may be true, we can also see his use of blue, orange, and other colors, and these combinations of colors serve to ⓔconceal his joy being conveyed.

Edward Hopper Van Gogh used yellow to express joy, but Edward Hopper’s use of yellow expresses loneliness. Hopper lived in New York City for nearly six decades, and he created paintings depicting urban scenes that showed how even ⓐfamiliar surroundings could cause the viewer to feel a sense of loneliness. Hopper’s Nighthawks is a ⓑgood example of this. There are four people in the same diner, but they’re clearly not ⓒapart. The bright yellow walls create a dramatic
ⓓresemblance to the darkness outside, emphasizing how people can be in the same space and feel apart. In Hopper’s Automat, the feeling of loneliness is even more ⓔdirect. The yellow lights lead the viewer’s eye to the yellow hat of the woman, and the cool shades of the other colors contrast with the warm yellow, emphasizing that she’s on her own.

다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오.
Asteroid Mining The solar system is composed of many rocks floating in space. The large ones are called planets, and the smaller ones are called asteroids. Research has shown that asteroids contain valuable resources like gold and rare earth elements. For example, one asteroid, 16 Psyche, is reported to consist mainly of gold and other precious metals, the value ⓐof which is equal to billions of dollars per person on Earth.
(A) No one knows for sure what asteroid mining will look like, but it seems that robotic mining is most likely. Robots will be sent to dig for target materials and send them back towards Earth. They will be programmed to explore the surface and identify materials, and be equipped for tasks such as drilling, collecting, and transporting. They may work independently or be controlled ⓑremote from Earth.
(B) Unfortunately, these types of robots have yet to be developed since the technology is still young. As technology continues to develop, better methods for obtaining materials will ⓒundoubtedly emerge.
(C) From a space explorers’ perspective, however, the most valuable resources from asteroids are neither valuable precious metals
ⓓor rare mineral deposits. That valuable resource could actually be water, and it seems to have been overlooked because it doesn’t seem as exciting as gold. Water is expensive to transport into space due to its weight and volume. would make space explorationsⓔmucheasier.

글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중 어법에 어색한 것 끼리 짝 지어진것은?
solution: ⓐ of which → 올바른 표현이다. 원문의 “whose value”를 관계대명사 구조로 바꾼 표현으로, the value of which : 그것들의 가치의 형태가 자연스럽게 사용되었다. ⓑ remote → 어법상 어색하다. 동사 controlled를 수식하려면 부사가 와야 하므로 remotely가 되어야 한다. be controlled remotely from Earth : 지구에서 원격으로 조종되다 ⓒ undoubtedly → 올바른 표현이다. 동사 emerge를 수식하는 부사로 적절하게 사용되었다. ⓓ or→ 어법상 어색하다. neither A nor B의 상관접속사 구문이 와야 하므로 or가 아니라 nor가 되어야 한다. neither valuable precious metals nor rare mineral deposits ⓔ much easier → 올바른 표현이다. 비교급 easier를 강조하는 부사 much가 적절하게 사용되었다. 따라서 어법상 어색한 것은 ⓑ, ⓓ이므로 정답은 ②이다.
